prior_importants.description: `pup ci wait` and `pup fix` now tell the operator to reply on an answered thread so the next round takes it again, but `fixRoundBrief` relays only the bot's first comment, so the worker gets the same finding with neither the operator's reply nor its earlier decline, and the round counts as a repeat-fix-round.

findings.description: Under a SUCCESS status, `pup ci wait` names `pup fix` whenever an unanswered, non-outdated thread exists, including one hidden on GitHub or edited by a non-bot account, which `reviewVerdict` always refuses; now that an earlier run's hidden-but-unresolved thread counts, ci wait sends the operator to a `pup fix` that cannot start a round instead of telling them to resolve it.

`isAnswered` is computed from only the newest 100 comments of a thread, so an outsider posting 100+ replies pushes pup's marked reply out of the `trail` window and makes an answered thread read unanswered, re-relaying a declined finding as a repeat-fix-round (contradicting ADR 0163's "an outsider's comment cannot reopen it"); reading `trail.pageInfo.hasPreviousPage` and leaving such a thread to the operator would fail closed.

The `FIX_ROUND_MARKER` JSDoc ("What every reply and comment a fix round posts ends on, before the round's sha") contradicts itself: the constant is the marker's prefix, which `fixRoundMarker` completes with the sha and `-->`, and which `isAnswered` matches.

The new inline comment on filtering answered threads in `reviewVerdict` restates what its JSDoc and `ReviewThread.isAnswered` already say (AGENTS.md §Comments: a WHY comment restating the seam's docs is a duplicate).

The `[cond && 'text', ...].filter((x): x is string => x !== false)` pattern, built in both reviewDigest and reviewVerdict (fix-round.service.ts:688-696), is harder to read than two `if` pushes into a `string[]`, which drop the false-sentinel and the type-guard lambda.

process_issues.description: The conventions reviewer checked only the ADR format and decision 90's amendment. It did not review the src/core source and test diffs against docs/conventions/general.md, naming.md or testing.md, and said its brief gave no clear scope for that pass, so conventions coverage of the code is partial this round.
